FXUS62 KRAH 111047
AFDRAH

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Raleigh NC
646 AM EDT Fri Sep 11 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...

* Heat indices 100-102 in the Triangle Area south and east to the 
  coast today. Best chance of storms in the northeast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 215 AM Friday...

1) Hot today with a chance of PM thunderstorms, especially north 
and east. 

2) A bit cooler Saturday, but high humidity and thunderstorms are 
expected.  

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 200 AM Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1... Hot today with a chance of PM thunderstorms, 
especially north and east. 

Expect the day to begin mostly sunny as the latest satellite and 
observational data depict mainly clear skies under the upper ridge 
over the SE states. Highs will reach the lower to mid 90s, with heat 
indices of 100-102 expected this afternoon, mainly from the eastern 
Piedmont through the Coastal Plain. 

A weak front to our north is expected to trigger scattered 
thunderstorms, mainly over VA this afternoon. The latest hi-res 
convection allowing models suggest that widely scattered to 
scattered thunderstorms will develop, mainly over the northern and 
eastern areas of central NC this afternoon, then linger into the 
evening. There may be a minimum of storm chances over the west-
central Piedmont (west of the pre-frontal trough). 

Very muggy lows tonight in the 70s are expected. 

KEY MESSAGE 2... A bit cooler Saturday, but high humidity and 
thunderstorms are expected.  

The approaching mid/upper disturbance and weakening trough will give 
us a glancing blow as it passes to our north on Saturday. A 
weakening cold front and previous days left over boundaries should 
focus a day when more numerous thunderstorms develop over the 
region. QPF is up this run a little from previous runs, but 50 
percent of the area may still remain less than 0.50 or less. PWs 
will be very high and this moisture will combine with surface 
heating into the mid 80s NW and 90 SE to produce MLCapes around 2000 
to 2500 j/kg SE. Locally heavy rain is expected, yet flash flooding 
should be isolated and limited to poor drainage areas. A few lucky 
areas will get 1 to 1.5 inches storm totals.

KEY MESSAGE 3... Lingering showers/storms mainly I-95 east on 
Sunday; otherwise, drier with temperatures closer to the 30 
year historical averages most of the upcoming week. 

There is a lingering chance of mainly PM showers/storms, especially 
around and east of I-95 Sunday. Otherwise, dry upper ridging will 
take control again Monday into Thursday. There is some good news as 
temperatures are expected to be closer to normal, with a surface 
high to our north and northeast bringing a light NE flow. Highs in 
general this week will be in the 80s, flirting with 90 in the east.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/... 
As of 646 AM Friday...

Most of central NC will remain VFR through the 24 hour TAF period. 
An exception this afternoon and evening will be the chance of a 
thunderstorm, mainly 18z-03z today/Sat. In addition, low stratus and 
some fog are likely between 09z and 13z/Saturday morning. 

Outlook: A period of two of showers/storms will be possible on 
Saturday, mainly in the afternoon and evening. Otherwise, generally 
VFR daytime conditions are expected Sunday into Tuesday.

Additionally, low stratus and/or fog may develop and cause sub-VFR 
restrictions early Sunday and early Monday mornings. 

&&

.RAH WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Badgett
AVIATION...Badgett

FXUS62 KILM 111032
AFDILM

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Wilmington NC
632 AM EDT Fri Sep 11 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Forecast for showers and thunderstorms remains in place this
weekend. The extended forecast has trended cooler.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Shower and thunderstorm chances will increase this weekend.

2) Heat and humidity will build and heat indices should exceed 
100 degrees through Monday.

3) Next week has trended cooler.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Shower and thunderstorm chances will increase 
this weekend.

IR satellite imagery shows the developing areas of moisture
across the southeast this morning and in the Missouri Valley
where the next mid level trough resides. The increase in 
moisture and forcing will lead to sea breeze driven activity 
early today then more of a scattered nature later in the day. 
The highest pops associated with this system/setup occur during 
the day Saturday and Sunday when likely values are in place. The
favored times are late morning and afternoons/evenings. There 
is a marginal risk for severe western areas today but otherwise 
the system...meandering in nature offers little in the way of 
shear and thus organized storms. 




KEY MESSAGE 2...Heat and humidity will build and heat indices should 
exceed 100 degrees through Monday. While actual temperatures
almost can't reach values of a few weeks ago due to the
continuing loss of daylight dewpoints reminiscent of a few 
weeks ago have returned and uncomfortable heat indices will 
develop for today through the weekend. No heat related headlines
are anticipated.


KEY MESSAGE 3...Guidance has shifted considerably from just a 
day or so ago when the heat mentioned in KEY MESSAGE 2 was 
supposed to continue. Now it appears the strong ridge (heat 
dome) remains to the west and our area remains under a cooler NE
flow. Highs still formidable just under 90 degrees will be 
tempered by lows in the middle 60s or so. Kinda similar to the 
past few days.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
VFR generally expected through most of the period. Some stratus
will continue to impact LBT over the next couple of hours.
Showers and storms develop this afternoon along the sea breeze
and gradually move inland, but will be of low enough coverage 
to maintain PROB30s, lower chance at ILM.

Extended Outlook... Although VFR conditions will prevail, there
is increasing potential for pop-up showers and thunderstorms
bringing brief MVFR/IFR conditions, especially Saturday and
Sunday. There is also a low potential for late night/early
morning stratus or ground fog, particularly affecting KLBT and
KFLO Saturday and Sunday.

&&

.MARINE...
Tonight through Wednesday...Very modest southwest winds will be
in place through the weekend as a sprawling relatively weak 
system moves across. By early next week after a day or two of a
weak pressure pattern a better defined NE flow develops. A 
decent surge with the arrival of the NE flow could warrant a 
close look at a small craft advisory but confidence especially 
this far out with surges is almost nil.

&&

.ILM WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
NC...Coastal Flood Advisory until noon EDT today for NCZ107.
SC...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

KEY MESSAGES...SHK
DISCUSSION...SHK
AVIATION...21
MARINE...SHK

FXUS62 KJAX 110654
AFDJAX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Jacksonville FL
254 AM EDT Fri Sep 11 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

For the latest NE FL and SE GA Daily Key Messages please visit:
https:/www.weather.gov/media/jax/briefings/nws-jax-briefing.pdf

- Daily Afternoon & Evening Thunderstorms. Main Hazards: Locally Heavy
  Rain, Lightning & Gusty Winds Up to 40-50 mph

- Moderate Rip Current Risk all Local Beaches Today through the
  weekend. Elevated Risk Returns Next Week

- Daily Heat Index up to 107 Each Afternoon through Sunday

&&

.NEAR TERM /TODAY THROUGH TONIGHT/... 
Main Highlights:

- Potential for isolated strong thunderstorms and localized flooding.

- Moderate Rip Current Risk at All Area Beaches.

Mean layer ridge oriented more or less west-east through 700 mb is 
located in central FL area. Typically, for September, this 
ridge is located further north. Deep layer flow is southwesterly
at about 10 kt, and we continue with the deep moisture in place
with the 18z JAX Sounding showing a PWAT of 2.29 inches and 500
mb temp of only -4.1C. Fairly confident PWATS will stay the 
same today, but the 500 mb temps may drop another degree or so 
during the day. Models suggest that some shortwave energy may 
impinge on the forecast area after 21z today which will likely 
encourage more cloudiness and probably boost rain chances this 
evening. 

Given the moisture and summer-like pattern, we anticipate scattered 
to numerous showers and storms to develop during the day. Initial 
development of convection likely to be around any lingering boundaries
from Thursday, and also along the west and east coast sea breezes
that develop by the early afternoon. Climatology would suggest 
the I-75 corridor first near the developing west coast sea breeze.
The movement of the west coast sea breeze may meet the east coast
sea breeze this afternoon and early evening, and cells mergers 
may would be near and east of the U.S. Highway 301 area. The 
moisture-laden airmass will be efficient for heavy rainfall/localized
flooding. Isolated rain amounts in excess of 3 inches in spots 
are likely. The DCAPE on the model soundings looks unimpressive 
at about 500-600 J/kg, similar to yesterday, so for now assuming
peak tstorm gusts of about 40-50 mph. Cannot totally rule out 
an isolated severe storm though where strongest convergence 
occurs. Scattered showers and storms expected in the evening 
and will fade overnight. Patchy fog again is possible this 
morning and early Saturday morning.

Daytime highs will be in the lower 90s, and probably around 90 at 
the east coast as the sea breeze develops. Heat index values will 
hover under Heat Advisory criteria, with values in the upper 90s to 
around 105F. Lows tonight in the lower to mid 70s.

&&

.SHORT TERM /SATURDAY THROUGH SUNDAY NIGHT/...
Main Highlights This Period:

- Potential for isolated strong thunderstorms and localized flooding 
on Saturday

Scattered to numerous showers and storms are anticipated on Saturday 
as moist southwesterly flow, with PWAT values of 2 to 2.3 inches, 
continues to move over the region from out of the Gulf. There is a 
potential for heavy rains and localized flooding for storms 
developing along the sea breeze boundaries and areas of convergence, 
likely along and west of the I-95 corridor. Convection is expected 
to be less widespread on Sunday as the high pressure ridge shifts 
northward and crosses over the forecast area, with the prevailing 
flow gradually shifting to a more northeasterly onshore flow by the 
beginning of next week. High temperatures will rise up into the 
lower 90s this weekend with overnight low temperatures dropping down 
into the lower to mid 70s over inland areas and int the mid to upper 
70s for areas along the coast. Heat index values today will rise to 
over 100 with apparent temperatures potentially reaching as high as 
110 for northeast Florida, however conditions are anticipated to 
remain below heat advisory criteria. Potential for patchy early 
morning fog and low cloud decks over inland areas before and around 
sunrise during the overnight and early morning hours this weekend.

&&

.LONG TERM /MONDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Main Highlights: 

- Daily Thunderstorms Potential Each Day Next Week

- Elevated Rip Current Risk Next Week 

Northeasterly onshore flow will be in place through the latter part 
of next week as the axis of high pressure rotation settles in to the 
north. Chances for daily bouts of showers and storms will lessen for 
southeast Georgia and areas of northeast Florida north of the I-10 
corridor as drier air advects into the forecast area from out of the 
northeast, with a higher likelihood of convection for areas south of 
I-10. Above average high temperatures reaching into the lower 90s 
will gradually drop down into the upper 80s and be nearer the 
seasonal average by midweek. Heat index values will drop down to be 
below 100.

Rip current risk will also become elevated rather than moderate as a 
result of the pattern shift.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z FRIDAY THROUGH 06Z SATURDAY/...
VFR clouds have returned to the area with all the showers done 
tonight. Light winds may allow for some cigs and vsby restrictions 
for VQQ and possibly GNV through 12Z.

Active convective day again with scattered to numerous showers and 
storms for all terminals this afternoon. TEMPO and PROB30 groups are 
in place for MVFR/IFR TSRA activity from 18-22Z, and little later 
for SSI. Expecting scattered TSRA at 22z so have continued some 
mention for TS through 02z Saturday. Movement of TSRA will be 
northeast up to around 10-15 kt. Convection will be winding down in 
the 02Z to 05Z time frame. Southwest winds near 4-8 kt expected to 
turn southeast for CRG, SGJ, and SSI after 16-18Z.

&&

.MARINE...

Atlantic high pressure ridge will be centered from Bermuda to 
central Florida through early next week. This will favor prevailing 
southwest to south winds the next few days but the afternoon sea 
breeze will shift winds to southeast each afternoon across the near 
shore waters. Thunderstorms will likely develop over coastal 
locations during the afternoon hours will shift eastward across our 
local waters during the late afternoon and evening hours through the 
weekend. Onshore winds are forecast to develop Tuesday, with breezy 
conditions and building seas forecast towards Tuesday and Wednesday 
of next week.

Rip Currents: Generally offshore flow and weakening surf conditions 
suggest continuing a moderate risk today, with a lingering 2 foot 
wind-sea swell of about 7-8 seconds. This trend continues into the 
weekend likely maintaining a low to moderate risk. An increased 
threat of dangerous rip currents possible on Tuesday into Wednesday.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...

Diurnal southwesterly winds will persist through the end of the week 
and through the weekend. As a result of the moist southwesterly 
flow, the diurnal east coast sea breeze will be pinned near the 
shoreline and not reach inland much past the I-95 corridor. Flow 
pattern is expected to shift to become more onshore by the beginning 
of next week.

Fog Potential: Gusty and erratic wind shifts will occur from 
thunderstorm activity. Patchy fog is expected across inland areas 
the next couple of mornings, with widespread dense fog unlikely.

&&

.HYDROLOGY...
As far as coastal water levels, coastal water levels will remain 
near and below action stage despite the new moon phase today.

As far as rainfall again today, isolated pockets of up to 3-4 inches 
are possible mainly the St Johns River Basin northward to near or 
just south of Waycross and Nahunta. These storms may cause temporary 
flooding, especially in any poor drainage or urbanized areas.

&&

.PRELIMINARY POINT TEMPS/POPS...
AMG  91  73  91  73 /  30  20  50  20 
SSI  90  77  89  76 /  30  20  50  20 
JAX  91  74  91  74 /  60  30  70  10 
SGJ  90  75  90  75 /  70  30  60  10 
GNV  91  73  91  73 /  60  20  70  20 
OCF  92  74  92  74 /  60  20  70  20 

&&

.JAX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
FL...None.
GA...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

FXUS65 KBOU 111132
AFDBOU

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Denver/Boulder CO
532 AM MDT Fri Sep 11 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Very warm today with only isolated high based showers/virga 
  late this afternoon and evening.

- Slight increase in shower/storm coverage this weekend. Cooler
  Saturday, then warmer Sunday.

- Unsettled pattern next week, with multiple cold fronts expected
  to bring a few more noticeable cooldowns.

&&

.DISCUSSION /Through Thursday/...
Issued at 231 AM MDT Fri Sep 11 2026

Zonal flow aloft will strengthen today, bringing a stronger
downslope component and thus a bit more warming. We expect highs 
to reach 90F or more over most of the plains and I-25 Corridor. 
To offset that, there is some mid/upper level moisture evident on 
satellite and radar now reaching northern Utah. This will continue
to push east today, resulting in enough for scattered virga,
isolated high based showers, and even a lone weak storm. The main
threat of any light precipitation would be over the northern 
mountains this afternoon, spreading to the northern plains this 
evening, but even there coverage would be sparse. Any high based 
showers/virga would support gusty outflow winds to 40 mph given 
increasing environmental flow and DCAPE increasing to 800-1200 
J/kg. 

For tonight, a cold front pushes south across the High Plains and
through northeast Colorado late tonight into early Saturday
morning. This will lead to cooler temperatures (near normal) for
Saturday. While moisture levels increase slightly, considerable
uncertainty exists for afternoon and evening shower/storm coverage
due to thermal profiles. For the most part, we don't think we'll
reach convective temps over the plains but still can't rule out
a few late day showers and storms spilling eastward from the
higher terrain due to mid level instability and moisture. 

Sunday will likely feature a return to much above normal
temperatures. MOS guidance suggest highs pushing into the mid 90s
for metro Denver and the I-25 Urban Corridor. That may be a bit
aggressive as there is some guidance (not surprisingly) slowing 
the redevelopment of lee troughing and erosion of low level
moisture. The record for Denver on the 13th is 96F set in 2018, 
1990, and 1895, but at this point it appears we'll most likely 
stay a couple degrees shy of that. With regard to convection, 
isolated showers and storms will be high based and relatively 
weak. However, if a storm or two can break the cap over the 
northeast plains they could certainly tap into higher MLCAPE and 
become severe. 

As discussed yesterday, the cooldown for Monday appears to be
tempered as the next cold front/upper trough has been delayed 
slightly. However, there is still high confidence in more 
significant cooling for Tuesday behind a moderately strong early 
(meteorological) autumn cold front. While daily uncertainties 
exist about the degree of cooling, there is modest agreement we'll
settle into highs in the 70s (and 30-40% chance of 60s) for the 
plains and I-25 Corridor. A brief warmup is possible for 
Wednesday before yet another front arrives Thursday. Ensembles are
in decent agreement holding a plume of mid/upper level moisture 
and higher than normal climatological precipitable water over us.
Thus, we should have daily chances of showers and storms most of 
the days this upcoming week. 

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS through 12Z Saturday/...
Issued at 532 AM MDT Fri Sep 11 2026

Main concern today is threat of gusty outflow winds from high
based virga/sprinkles 22Z-03Z. Given upstream satellite imagery
and radar returns, we believe there is enough moisture to warrant
at least a chance of gusty outflow winds. DCAPE is expected to
grow to 800-1200 J/kg and environmental winds are also increasing
today. There is uncertainty, however, if we fully reach 
convective temperature. For now, we added a PROB30 VRB G30kts to 
the TAFs to account for this potential with the main risk 23Z-02Z. 

Otherwise, VFR conditions will persist. Light S-SW winds will
become Light and variable toward 16Z. There is still some 
uncertainty in prevailing wind direction by 20Z, with a battle 
between diurnal upslope and stronger westerlies trying to advance 
off the foothills. For now, we've kept a N-NE component at KDEN 
and KAPA, with a more W-NW wind likely at KBJC. Winds will
eventually settle to more SE-S-SW 02Z-06Z. A weak cool front is
then expected to arrive 10Z-12Z Saturday, which should push winds
to the NW-N-NE through early Saturday morning.

&&

.BOU WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
None.

&&

$$
